Beginning early Tuesday morning, a warm front will lifts northward

values are forecast to surge upwards of 2.00-2.25 behind the front. 
As this front lifts north, hi res guidance continues to show

80 corridors across northeast PA and northern NJ, some areas of 
which were hit hard with flash flooding just this past weekend. At 
some point, the warm front will stall nearby the NJ/NY/PA border, 
but it is uncertain where. The area of greatest flash flood risk 
will likely be where the front stalls. A general 1-2 inches of rain 
can be expected from this first of many rounds of precipitation with 
locally higher amounts. While this may not sound significant, many 
locations, especially in northern NJ, remain vulnerable to excessive 
rainfall after this past weekend. As such, rainfall rates of 1-2 
inches per hour at times will be sufficient to result in scattered 
incidents of flash flooding during the critical morning rush hour 
Tuesday. Furthermore, there is a nonzero severe threat with these 
storms given the deep layer shear present along with the presence of
